answers.question: What is the Azure resource provider namespace and resource type of an Azure DocumentDB cluster?
answers.answer: Resource provider namespace: Microsoft.DocumentDB. Resource type: Microsoft.DocumentDB/databaseAccounts (e.g. resource id: /subscriptions/<sub>/resourceGroups/<rg>/providers/Microsoft.DocumentDB/databaseAccounts/<accountName>).

answers.question: Which Azure CLI command group creates and manages a cluster? Is it in the core CLI or an extension?
answers.answer: Use the built-in (core) CLI group az cosmosdb. Example: az cosmosdb create --name myAccount --resource-group myRg --locations regionName=westus --kind MongoDB. (No separate extension required in current az releases.)

answers.question: Which Bicep and Terraform resource types deploy a cluster?
answers.answer: Bicep/ARM resource type: Microsoft.DocumentDB/databaseAccounts (e.g. resource cosmos 'Microsoft.DocumentDB/databaseAccounts@2021-06-15' = { name: 'myAccount' properties: { kind: 'MongoDB' ... } }). Terraform: use resource "azurerm_cosmosdb_account" "example" { name = "myAccount" location = azurerm_resource_group.rg.location offer_type = "Standard" kind = "MongoDB" ... }.

answers.question: What does a connection string look like: scheme, host suffix, port, and the options it must carry?
answers.answer: MongoDB-style connection string. Example (TLS): mongodb://<username>:<password>@<account>.mongo.cosmos.azure.com:10255/?ssl=true&replicaSet=globaldb&retryWrites=false&appName=@<account>@. Host suffix: .mongo.cosmos.azure.com. TLS/SSL port: 10255 (the TLS/SSL MongoDB port for Cosmos DB Mongo API). Options normally include ssl=true (or tls=true), replicaSet=globaldb and retryWrites=false.

answers.question: How is capacity provisioned and billed: request units, compute tiers with vCores, serverless, or something else?
answers.answer: Primary billing model is Azure Cosmos DB RUs (Request Units) + storage. You can provision throughput (RUs/sec) at database/collection level or use serverless (pay-per-request, where available). There are newer managed MongoDB-like SKUs in Azure that use instance sizes (M-series/vCore) for compatibility, but the common/Azure-native model is RU-based provisioned or serverless.

answers.question: Which authentication methods are supported, and how does a driver authenticate with Microsoft Entra ID?
answers.answer: For the MongoDB API you normally authenticate with Mongo-style credentials (username/password) provided by the Cosmos DB account (SCRAM-style) or use the account connection string (account key) in the URI. Microsoft Entra ID (Azure AD) authentication is supported for some Cosmos DB APIs (SQL/Table) via RBAC, but for the MongoDB API there is no general Azure AD-backed MongoDB driver authentication; drivers use the Mongo credentials/connection string. (If AAD support is required, use an API that supports AAD or a proxy.)

answers.question: Which client library should an application use? Is there a service-specific SDK?
answers.answer: For apps use the standard MongoDB drivers (e.g. pymongo for Python). The MongoDB wire protocol compatibility means no service-specific application driver is required. For management tasks use the Azure management SDKs (azure-mgmt-cosmosdb / az cli).

answers.question: Which vector index types are supported, and what does the command that creates one look like?
answers.answer: If the cluster exposes vector indexes it uses algorithm types such as HNSW, IVF or DiskANN (service-dependent). The create-index pattern is non-standard to MongoDB and looks like a special vector index command. Example (best-effort concrete guess): db.products.createIndex({ embeddings: "vector" }, { algorithm: "hnsw", dims: 1536, metric: "cosine" }). Note: the exact index option names vary by service; confirm with the cluster's index API/management tools.

answers.question: How are full-text search and hybrid search done?
answers.answer: Simple full-text search: use MongoDB text indexes (db.collection.createIndex({ field: 'text' })). For richer/hybrid text+vector search integrate with Azure Cognitive Search or the service's vector-search feature (if available) which can combine text scoring and vector similarity. Cosmos DB does not automatically provide the same hybrid search features as dedicated search services—use Cognitive Search or the provider's vector-search extension.

answers.question: Which MongoDB wire protocol or server versions are supported, and which commonly used MongoDB features are not?
answers.answer: Supported wire protocol versions depend on account configuration; recent managed accounts support MongoDB server versions up to 6.0–7.0 (e.g. MongoDB 7.0 wire protocol) depending on the SKU. Common unsupported or limited features vs upstream MongoDB: some admin/replica-set ops, direct oplog access, certain server-side JS ($where), unsupported or limited server commands, and some aggregation operators or behaviors may differ. Always check the account's supported server version and feature matrix before depending on advanced MongoDB features.

answers.question: How do you run the database locally for development and tests: which image or emulator, and which port?
answers.answer: There is no full emulator for the MongoDB API of Cosmos DB. For local development run a MongoDB server (official image) to exercise the MongoDB driver compatibility: docker run -p 27017:27017 --name mongo -d mongo:7.0 and connect via mongodb://localhost:27017. For Cosmos DB-specific behavior test against the real cluster (or use Azure Cosmos DB emulator for SQL API only).

answers.question: Are change streams supported, and does anything have to be enabled first?
answers.answer: Change streams for the MongoDB API have historically been limited or unavailable. If you need change notifications on Cosmos DB use Cosmos DB Change Feed (SQL API) or check the account's MongoDB server-version compatibility for change-stream support. In short: assume change streams are not generally available unless your specific account version explicitly advertises support; prefer the Cosmos Change Feed for guaranteed support.

answers.question: Which MCP server gives an agent data-plane tools for this service? Does the general Azure MCP Server cover it?
answers.answer: Use the documentdb MCP server (documentdb profile) for data-plane inspection and tooling for Cosmos DB/Mongo API. The general Azure MCP server does not replace the service-specific documentdb MCP server tooling; use the documentdb profile to inspect collections, indexes and query plans.

answers.question: What was this service called before, and how does it relate to Azure Cosmos DB and to the open-source DocumentDB project?
answers.answer: Azure DocumentDB was the original name/early incarnation of what is now Azure Cosmos DB. The Azure 'DocumentDB' name historically referred to Microsoft’s managed JSON/document database service that evolved and was rebranded to Cosmos DB. It is Microsoft’s proprietary managed service and is not the same as any unrelated open-source project named DocumentDB.

answers.question: What engine is underneath, and does that change anything in application code?
answers.answer: Under the MongoDB API the underlying engine is Azure Cosmos DB's proprietary storage/engine that translates MongoDB wire protocol operations into Cosmos storage operations. For application code you mainly use standard MongoDB drivers, but you must account for service differences (throughput/RU model, some unsupported server features, different consistency/transaction guarantees and query planner behaviors). Expect small compatibility gaps; test your queries against the actual cluster.

answers.question: What connection string environment variable and exact form will the sample read at runtime?
answers.answer: The sample will read DOCUMENTDB_URI from the environment. Expected form: mongodb://<username>:<password>@<account>.mongo.cosmos.azure.com:10255/?ssl=true&replicaSet=globaldb&retryWrites=false&appName=@<account>@. Do not hard-code credentials; read DOCUMENTDB_URI at runtime (or from a .env file) and pass it to pymongo.MongoClient(DOCUMENTDB_URI).

answers.question: Which database name must the sample use?
answers.answer: Use the database name sample_customer_360_12 for all collections and operations created/used by this sample.

answers.question: Which Python packages and install command will the sample instruct the developer to install?
answers.answer: Install the runtime deps with pip. Example: pip install pymongo==4.* langchain openai python-dotenv. (If you use specific vector/embedding libs or the service SDK add them. For agent tools you may add faiss or sentence-transformers only if you run local vector ops — for this sample we rely on DocumentDB vector search so not required.)

answers.question: What aggregation pipeline will the DocumentDB aggregation tool run to compute purchase frequency, average order value and tenure per customer?
answers.answer: Use a MongoDB aggregation pipeline. Example pipeline (use in pymongo as list): [ { $match: { status: { $ne: 'cancelled' } } }, { $group: { _id: '$customer_id', orders_count: { $sum: 1 }, total_spent: { $sum: '$order_total' }, avg_order_value: { $avg: '$order_total' }, first_order: { $min: '$order_date' }, last_order: { $max: '$order_date' } } }, { $addFields: { tenure_days: { $dateDiff: { startDate: '$first_order', endDate: '$$NOW', unit: 'day' } }, avg_order_value: '$avg_order_value', orders_count: '$orders_count' } } ]. Run this against the orders collection and join/update against the customers collection as needed.

answers.question: What update command will the sample use to write the CLV score, tier and rationale back to the customer profile document?
answers.answer: Use a standard updateOne call. Example pymongo code: customers.update_one({ '_id': customer_id }, { '$set': { 'clv.score': clv_score, 'clv.tier': clv_tier, 'clv.rationale': clv_rationale, 'clv.updated_at': datetime.utcnow() } }) . Replace customer_id with the document _id. Do not upsert unless you intend to create missing profiles.
